summary: All six runtime contracts hold at 1ea3d5db. Every close-path caller tolerates the new fields (no destructuring or strict shape validation; orchestrator isStop keys off a status field the close result never had). review violations parses --id/--json, errors on missing --id, exits 2 only on unacknowledged entries; review close stays exit 0 when it records a violation, matching Spec C-002. gate:review_surface_integrity is spelled from a single exported constant everywhere, has both edges outside the fast-lane ternary, is registered in nodes/requiredGates/collectUnresolvedRequiredGates, and reaches execution_gate.blocking_gates via the failed-status fallthrough with a remediation command whose every flag and enum exists in the CLI. VIBEPRO_REVIEW_SURFACE_LEDGER_UNREADABLE is dispatched on error.code at its single catch site with no bare catch swallowing it. runtimeStopCloseReason can only emit timeout or manual_shutdown, both recognized, so the orchestrator can never trip assertRecognizedCloseReason. The one real runtime weakness - the mkdir lock stale reclaim is check-then-act - fails closed rather than corrupting (a raced-away entry resurfaces as a blocking missing:<id> reconciliation violation) and 240 concurrent appends against a pre-planted stale lock lost nothing. Two low findings, neither a contract break.

findings.detail: withDirectoryLock stale reclaim is check-then-act and the finally-rm deletes whatever directory is at the lock path, so two waiters racing a stale lock can both enter the read-modify-write and drop one entry; fails closed via pointer reconciliation (blocking missing:<id> violation) but the emitted detail then wrongly accuses ledger tampering; fix is an atomic rename-based reclaim plus a holder token checked before the finally-rm

review violations calls readers directly without requireStoryId or assertInitializedWorkspace; missing --id errors without naming the flag, and an uninitialized workspace reports readable true with zero violations and exit 0, a positive claim the gate path itself refuses to make

finding_dispositions.reason: fail-closed impact bounded by pointer reconciliation; empirically unreproducible in 240 probed concurrent appends; fix (atomic rename reclaim + holder token) is a focused follow-up outside this frozen review surface
CLI ergonomics gap with no downstream dependency (gate path asserts initialization via pr prepare); follow-up alongside the reporting-only replay finding from the gate-stage review

judgment_delta: initial expected at least one needs_changes-grade break, with the 30s stale-lock reclaim as prime suspect for silent record loss and the new required gate as prime suspect for newly blocking unrelated PRs -> final pass because (a) the reclaim TOCTOU failure mode is fail-closed: the lifecycle pointer lives in a different file, so a raced-away entry reappears as a blocking missing:<id> reconciliation violation, and 240 probed concurrent appends lost nothing; (b) the blocking needs_evidence branch of buildReviewSurfaceIntegrityGate is unreachable in pr prepare since summarizeAgentReviewsForPr returns null only for a falsy storyId and buildPrContext always has one, so zero-review stories pass; (c) both close write paths, the CLI, and the full orchestrator stop-reason enumeration were checked against the recognized set rather than assumed.
